review_type: Independent adversarial mathematical and primary-source review; private only.
paper: Hu et al., Towards Optimal Multi-draft Speculative Decoding, ICLR2025

source_locations.location: Final printed p.4, Eq6 and Section2.3
source_locations.fact: Drafts are successively sampled from original q with previously selected token masses excluded and the remainder renormalized. Acceptance is output membership in any of the n drafts, with only the required marginals.
General optimum is1+min_H(P(H)-Pr(all drafts in H)). The witness does not refute this general identity.
Algorithm scans prefixes sorted by q/p and substitutes e_n(q_H)/e_n(q) for the all-in-H probability.

source_locations.location: Final printed p.17, proof of Theorem4
source_locations.fact: The same probability identity begins the q-convexity proof. Its failure invalidates this proof step, not by itself the q-convexity statement.
The RRS comparison separately uses successive exclusion/renormalization, confirming the sequential protocol is operationally used in the mathematical baseline.

author_defenses.defense: Without replacement means iid draws conditioned on an entirely distinct batch.
author_defenses.adjudication: This repairs the elementary-symmetric formula, but changes the explicit Eq6 law. The positive control gives exactly19/20 under that alternative law. It is a change of mathematical problem, not a reconciliation of the stated sequential protocol.

author_defenses.defense: The distinction is only ordered versus unordered tuples.
author_defenses.adjudication: Fails. The all-in-H event is invariant under order and its probability is1/20 for Eq6 versus1/10 for the substituted law.

author_defenses.defense: q is an adjusted weighting rather than the original draft distribution.
author_defenses.adjudication: No such transformation is specified. Eq6, the generating function and the q/p ordering use the same q. Introducing another parameterization would require a new equivalence and algorithm argument.

author_defenses.defense: The witness verifier is inadmissible or tuned to p.
author_defenses.adjudication: Fails under the stated definitions: every fixed p,q pair is permitted; the deterministic selection kernel has precisely target marginal p and always outputs a draft. No online-first-only constraint is present.

author_defenses.defense: The computation may be an approximation rather than an upper bound.
author_defenses.adjudication: The text explicitly presents an exact optimum/upper-bound computation. Its19/20 value lies below a feasible100% kernel and below the paper-defined RRS baseline at191/200.

author_defenses.defense: The unpublished experimental implementation may have used a different or corrected law.
author_defenses.adjudication: Possible and unresolved. The finite result does not establish how the published empirical table was computed or quantify its correction.

centrality: Nontrivial failure of the claimed efficient exact acceptance computation for the stated successive-without-replacement case. This is one of the paper's central proposed diagnostics, rather than a typographic change with identical numerical behavior.
limits: No disproof of q-convexity itself for successive sampling.
No disproof of the conditional prefix theorem given q-convexity.
No disproof of the general optimal-transport/subset formulation.
With-replacement results and the distinct Greedy draft protocol are outside the counterexample.
No empirical table, real-model speedup, or frequency of the mismatch has been recalculated.
No claim of novelty priority or complete prior-art clearance.
recommendation: Suitable for a precise private correction candidate with the stated scope. Any flagship/public novelty characterization still requires appropriate prior-status review and separate authorization.
